rust.error: document type declarations are not supported

reason: fast-xml-parser reads a document type declaration and expands the internal entities it declares; that reader (DocTypeReader.js with xml-naming and is-unsafe, about 400 lines) is not ported. Rust refuses the fragment, and that is the decided end state: the Open Packaging Conventions forbid DTDs in a package part. No tracked document has a DOCTYPE in a part the engine parses.

rust.error: a surrogate pair would be split

reason: fast-xml-parser takes the nine UTF-16 units after any '<![' as the CDATA opener, so a malformed opener can cut a character outside the BMP in half and leave a lone surrogate in the text. A Rust string cannot hold a lone surrogate. Rust refuses the fragment instead of inventing a replacement character.

JSZip has two UTF-8 decoders. Where a global Buffer exists (Node: CLI, tests, main process) it replaces each ill-formed sequence with U+FFFD, which is what Rust does and what the gate compares. Where none exists (a browser, and the sandboxed desktop renderer unless a bundler supplies one) it uses pako's decoder, which never rejects a byte: stray continuation bytes become control characters, a lead byte swallows the bytes after it, encoded surrogates stay lone surrogates, and the result depends on where JSZip's 16 KiB blocks end. The TypeScript engine therefore already reads ill-formed parts differently per host. Rust follows the Node behaviour everywhere. Every .xml and .rels entry of the tracked documents is well-formed UTF-8, so no tracked document is affected.

The TypeScript tables are plain objects, so a lookup by a value from the document also answers to the keys every object inherits: __proto__ gives Object.prototype, and constructor, toString, valueOf and hasOwnProperty give functions. A caller that tests the result for truth then stores it: directPLayer sets the paragraph align to it for a w:jc whose w:val is constructor. The Rust tables answer only to their own keys. The gate leaves these keys out of the two table comparisons and checks them here.
See table-lookup-inherited-key-object. A function result is invisible in JSON, which is how a parsed model would lose the field without a trace.
See table-lookup-inherited-key-object: the same lookup on the East Asian default font table.

typescript.refused: zip rejected: part word/styles.xml cannot be inflated: TypeError

rust.refused: zip rejected: part word/styles.xml cannot be inflated: the deflate data is damaged or cut short

reason: The zip gate ends this message with the text of the error DecompressionStream rejects with. That text belongs to the host: Node 22 rejects with a TypeError whose message is empty, so the gate falls back to its name, and a browser words it differently. Rust writes one sentence of its own. The gate compares the message up to "cannot be inflated:", which is the part the TypeScript wrote.

container: zip64 extensible data that reads itself again

rust.refused: Corrupted zip: the ZIP64 extensible data does not end

reason: JSZip 3.10.1 reads the extensible data of a ZIP64 end record in a loop whose counter never advances (zipEntries.js, readBlockZip64EndOfCentral): it ends when a read runs past the data. A field whose length is -6 moves the reader back to the start of the field, so the loop reads the same six bytes for ever and loadDocxZip never returns. The zip gate does not stop the archive: it refuses ZIP64 by the record count, the directory size and offset, and a locator 20 bytes before the end record, while JSZip also takes a disk number of 0xffff as ZIP64 and finds the locator anywhere. Rust refuses the container. This is a defect of the TypeScript engine (a document that hangs the application), reported with unit 1c, not behaviour to reproduce. Expected to go stale: main's zip gate refuses the container since d49361a3f (it refuses all six end-record fields JSZip reads as ZIP64). Once this branch holds that commit the TypeScript side refuses, the gate reports this entry as stale, and the entry goes together with the same rule in the Rust gate.

container: zip64 extensible data that leads back over two fields

rust.refused: Corrupted zip: the ZIP64 extensible data does not end

reason: The same loop as zip64-extensible-data-never-ends, entered another way: a field of length 0 followed by one of length -12 that ends where the first began. No single field ends where it started, so a reader that only compares a field's end with its own start reads the two for ever, as JSZip does. Rust keeps the starts of the fields it has read and refuses the container at the first one it meets again. Listed apart from the one-field container because the first Rust port refused that one and still hung on this one. Expected to go stale with it, for the same reason.

See table-lookup-inherited-key-object. parseStyles lower-cases the w:lang w:eastAsia of the docDefaults and looks it up in EA_LANG_DEFAULT_FONT. For constructor (and __proto__) the TypeScript takes the inherited member for a font: it stores a function as eastAsiaFont and sets eaFromLang. The lower-casing keeps toString, valueOf and hasOwnProperty out. The Rust table answers for its own keys only, so neither field is set.
See table-lookup-inherited-key-object: symbol-fonts.ts asks whether a font is a symbol font with `in` on the table of code pages, which also holds for every inherited key.
See table-lookup-inherited-key-symbol-font: the font passes the test, its code page is a function, and a lookup of the code in it finds nothing, so the character is returned as it is instead of null.
See table-lookup-inherited-key-symbol-char, through symbolGlyph.
See table-lookup-inherited-key-symbol-char, through decodeSymbolText.
See table-lookup-inherited-key-object: the table of bullet substitutes in list-markers.ts, read with the level text of a bullet.
See table-lookup-inherited-key-symbol-font: a font taken for a symbol font gets no fallback face.
See table-lookup-inherited-key-bullet: where the lookup lands in a document. A bullet whose level text is constructor gets a function as its marker.

decodeXmlText (zotero-doc-props.ts) turns a character reference into String.fromCodePoint of its number without refusing the surrogate range, so a reference to half of a pair leaves a lone surrogate in the text. A Rust string cannot hold one: Rust decodes into UTF-16 units and replaces a unit without its pair by U+FFFD, which is what the text becomes anyway the first time it is written as UTF-8. Two references that form a pair combine on both sides. Comparison (f) compares every case whose TypeScript result holds a lone surrogate with those units written as U+FFFD, so the rest of the result is still checked, and this entry holds the raw difference.
See lone-surrogate-from-a-character-reference: the same decoding, here in the key of the custom properties record.

See table-lookup-inherited-key-object: the table of VML colour names in parse-vml.ts, read with the fillcolor of a shape. Through readWatermarkShape a watermark whose fillcolor is constructor gets a function as its colour, where Rust gives the default 000000.

rust.error: the options argument: unknown variant `constructor`, expected `A4` or `Letter`

reason: See table-lookup-inherited-key-object: buildBlankDocx reads the page size from a table by options.paperSize. For an inherited key the entry is a function, its width and height are undefined, and the document is written with w:w="undefined". The type allows only A4 and Letter, so this needs a caller that passes an unchecked string. Rust refuses any other paper size.

The LaTeX reader of math.ts moves in UTF-16 units and takes one unit as the argument of ^, _ and of a command without braces, so a character outside the BMP is cut in half: its first half becomes the argument and its second half the next atom, each a lone surrogate in the OMML. Rust reads the same units and writes U+FFFD for each half. See lone-surrogate-from-a-character-reference for how the gate treats these cases.

latexToOmml recurses once per group and the TypeScript runs until the JavaScript stack overflows, somewhere past a thousand levels depending on the host. A stack overflow in wasm ends the instance, so Rust counts the depth and refuses past 256 levels of its reader (128 nested groups). No formula a person writes is that deep; the limit is listed because the two sides answer differently between the two limits.
